rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to evaluate if combining RNA and image data improves performance. This configuration isolates the effect of multimodal fusion (concat) and single-profile settings, providing critical insight into whether multimodal approaches are worth further exploration. It balances simplicity with key design choices (encoders, fusion) to inform subsequent experiments efficiently.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, no aggregation, concat fusion) achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (config_017) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It directly addresses a key design choice (fusion type) while keeping other parameters consistent, providing critical insight into whether weighted fusion is better than concatenation for this task.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve moderate performance. This experiment tests changing the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 (a different representation) while keeping other settings identical (singleprofile, resnet50, aggregation=None, fusion=concat). This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder, a critical design choice, to determine if it significantly impacts performance. It balances exploration (testing a new encoder) with exploitation (using the same effective setup as top-performing models).

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder (config_028) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.5362). This experiment tests whether extending to multiprofile (a key design choice) with avgpool aggregation (a new method) improves performance, while keeping the RNA and image encoders consistent. This isolates the impact of profile setting and aggregation, which are critical but untested in the current top-performing configuration.

Existing evidence shows that config_030 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.6315). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (config_031) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. Since config_030's success may depend on aggregation and encoder choices, testing a key variant (fusion type) provides critical insights without altering other factors, balancing exploitation of promising directions with exploration of design decisions.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (instead of avgpool) in the same setup isolates the impact of aggregation method, a critical design choice. It leverages the strong evidence from config_031 to explore a logical extension, balancing exploitation of promising directions with exploration of key variables.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a larger, more complex model) with the same RNA encoder and fusion settings improves performance. It isolates the impact of the image encoder choice, a key design decision, while maintaining consistency in other critical components.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt in this high-performing setup improves accuracy, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder. It balances exploitation (building on a strong baseline) and exploration (testing a novel encoder).

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_039). This experiment tests whether the multiprofile setting alone (without image data) benefits RNA-only models with transformer aggregation, isolating the impact of profile setting and aggregation. It clarifies if multiprofile is a general improvement or specific to multimodal models, providing critical insight under limited budget.

Existing evidence shows high performance with multimodal multiprofile models using scgpt, vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039: 0.725 accuracy). This experiment tests whether changing fusion from weighted to concat (while keeping other parameters the same) impacts performance, isolating the effect of fusion method. It is informative for determining optimal fusion strategies without overcomplicating the model.
